therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: dopaminergic modulation of mood and sensorimotor symptoms
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: adults with moderate to severe idiopathic restless legs syndrome with mild depression
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Average change in MADRS total score from baseline to week 12

results.effect_size: Mean difference -3.6 points (95% CI: -5.6 to -1.6) on MADRS
subgroup_findings: In participants with MADRS >= 18 at baseline: ropinirole -12.5 vs placebo -8.8
In participants with HAM-D >= 15 at baseline: ropinirole -9.6 vs placebo -7.2
In participants with BDI >= 21 at baseline: ropinirole -10.9 vs placebo -9.9
In participants with major depressive episodes (DSM criteria): MADRS ropinirole -11.6 vs placebo -7.6
IRLS change at 12 weeks: ropinirole -14.6 vs placebo -10.2
74.9% ropinirole vs 48.3% placebo achieved >=6 point decrease in MADRS at 12 weeks
11.7% ropinirole vs 23.3% placebo had MADRS >= 18 at week 12
10.7% ropinirole vs 26.8% placebo had HAM-D >= 15 at week 12
safety_signals: Serious adverse events were infrequent; back pain, pulmonary embolism, nausea, vomiting, bronchitis, and missed abortion each occurred in 1/197 ropinirole patients
